title: Bakken micro-balance
as_of_note: Production Aug 2026 (ND DMR). Montana Bakken Jul 2026 (state board well-grain rollup). Saskatchewan Viewfield Jul 2026 (pool file). Rail Jul 2026 (EIA). Dakota Access flow is the CY2024 Form 6 average. Refining per EIA-820, Jan 1 2026. Capacities as of Oct 2026.
units: kb/d unless a field name says otherwise

supply.label: ND Bakken and Three Forks production
supply.source: ND DMR county/formation monthly file (held, micro_balances/sources/north_dakota_dmr/)
supply.note: Formation total for Bakken and Three Forks together, from the NDIC well file (production is the Runs column). Printed pool rows sum to about 1,002 kb/d; the balance is confidential-well runs (about 131 kb/d in Aug 2026) allocated to the formation, which closes the formation to the NDIC formation series within about 0.3%. The allocation is labelled as an allocation, never printed as measurement.

supply.label: ND conventional and other production
supply.source: ND DMR county/formation monthly file (held, micro_balances/sources/north_dakota_dmr/)
supply.note: State total of record (1,161.4) minus the Bakken and Three Forks formation total (1,132.9). Small, slow-declining streams gathered into the same systems.

supply.label: Montana Bakken production (Williston counties)
supply.source: Montana Board of Oil and Gas well files, six Williston counties, rolled up monthly (held, micro_balances/sources/other_states/montana_bakken_rollup_monthly.csv)
supply.note: Well-grain Bakken-formation slice for the Montana Williston. Supersedes the earlier whole-state EIA proxy (79 kb/d, CY2025 average), which counted non-Williston Montana output. The six-county well sum runs 82.5-92.3% of the EIA Montana state total; the remainder is non-Williston production and coverage difference.

supply.label: Saskatchewan Bakken production (Viewfield pool)
supply.source: Saskatchewan Monthly Production by Pool workbooks (held, micro_balances/sources/saskatchewan/sk_viewfield_bakken_pool_monthly.csv)
supply.note: Viewfield Bakken Sand Pool: 19,174 b/d in Jul 2026 (8,413 from named units plus 10,761 on the pool-level row). Part of the basin frame; it gathers north to Cromer and enters the Enbridge Mainline pool. Well-level Saskatchewan production is a paid IRIS product and is not held.

supply.label: Manitoba Bakken (memo, loads at Cromer)
supply.source: Manitoba provincial data (via Bakken Formation compilation)
supply.note: Memo item: excluded from the supply card. 38.5 kb/d in 2023, down from 42.1 in 2020. No formation-level Manitoba series is held.

demand.label: Dakota Access to Patoka
demand.source: FERC Form 6 Schedule 600 sample parse (held, micro_balances/sources/ferc_form6/), Dakota Access LLC filing
demand.note: The one hard pipe flow number held: 223.53 MMbbl received from North Dakota origins, 223.36 MMbbl delivered out in CY2024, an average of about 611 kb/d, 81% of nameplate. Dakota Access is 55% of the basin's pipe egress nameplate. Expansion status, corrected Oct 2026: the often-cited increase to about 1.1 MMb/d was a 2019 plan; the completed optimization phase reached the current 750 kb/d in Aug 2021, and no further Dakota Access expansion is a live project (Dakota Access North, 250 kb/d, was dropped from Energy Transfer's Q2 2026 deck backlog with no FID). The basin's live pipe growth item is the proposed Bridger Pipeline Expansion, about 550 kb/d from the Canadian border to Guernsey, in permitting.

demand.label: ETCO onward: Patoka to Gulf Coast
demand.source: FERC Form 6, Dakota Access LLC delivery rows (partial evidence only)
demand.note: Dakota Access and ETCO are marketed as one Bakken system. The Form 6 delivery rows show the shape (126.6 MMbbl terminated on its own Illinois trunk lines, 96.7 MMbbl delivered out to connecting carriers in CY2024) but ETCO capacity was not verified from a primary source in the dossier pass (commonly cited near 570-600, not printed).

demand.label: Enbridge North Dakota system to Clearbrook
demand.source: Enbridge factsheets (Line 81 average annual capacity); carrier Form 6 in the held filer universe, not yet parsed
demand.note: The original egress, operating since the 1950s-60s. Historically ran near full before Dakota Access; no current public flow. Nameplate is the Line 81 average annual figure.

demand.label: Enbridge Bakken North to Cromer (Mainline)
demand.source: CER pipeline profile; East Daley Crude Oil Edge (utilization)
demand.note: Reversed in 2013 to carry Bakken crude north into the Mainline at Cromer. CER prints 145 kb/d, East Daley 149. Utilization ran about 7-26% in 2023: it is the relief valve and the most expensive routine option (about $6/bbl toll versus about $2.56 on the Enbridge ND system, East Daley tariff comparison), so its utilization is a clean tightness gauge for the northern light complex.

demand.label: High Plains to Mandan refinery
demand.source: GEM wiki citing Tesoro Logistics (trunk capacity); EIA-820 refinery capacity file, Jan 1 2026 (Mandan 72,000 b/cd calendar day, 76,500 stream day)
demand.note: About 90 kb/d trunk on a 700-mile gathering system feeding Marathon's Mandan refinery. Mandan is North Dakota's only crude refinery: 72 kb/d calendar-day capacity in the EIA-820 file dated Jan 1, 2026 (older citations of 74-76 are superseded). Refinery crude runs are not published monthly. Operating status after the Fort Berthold right-of-way litigation needs a build-stage check.

demand.label: Butte Pipe Line to Guernsey
demand.source: ND PSC filing (Bentek study); Bridger Pipeline LLC Form 6 in the held universe, not yet parsed
demand.note: The only southbound pipe out of the Montana side, expanded to 150 kb/d in 2011. Carries Montana Bakken and North Dakota barrels gathered to Baker. Flows are not published. Capacity evidence has widened since the 2011 figure: the North Dakota Pipeline Authority's 2024 annual report states the Butte system at 275 kb/d to Guernsey, and East Daley (May 2026, from FERC filings) cites a 285 kb/d nameplate with actual shipments of about 317 kb/d in Q3 2025 and about 340 kb/d in Q4 2025, after Double H left crude service (drag-reducing agents are East Daley's inferred mechanism). The 150 kb/d carried here is the filed 2011 expansion nameplate; the spread between filed nameplate and demonstrated throughput is printed, not resolved.

demand.label: Rail to West Coast (PADD 5)
demand.note: EIA lane: PADD 2 origin to PADD 5. The PADD 2 origin lane is overwhelmingly Bakken loadings plus a small non-Bakken Midwest residual. In the current loose-pipe regime, rail volumes are set by West Coast refinery demand for Bakken light sweet, not by basin egress stress.

demand.label: Rail to East Coast (PADD 1)
demand.note: The 2013-15 pattern (marginal rail barrel east to Brent-priced refineries) has flipped: the East Coast lane is now a residual.

demand.label: Rail to Gulf and other (PADD 3 and intra)
demand.note: Small residual lanes from PADD 2 origins.

demand.label: Montana refining cluster (memo, shared demand pool)
demand.dest: Billings, Laurel and Great Falls, Montana
demand.source: EIA refinery capacity table (Jan 2026), via secondary source
demand.note: Memo item: ExxonMobil Billings, Phillips 66 Billings, CHS Laurel and Calumet Great Falls, about 210 kb/d combined. The cluster runs mostly Canadian crude plus Montana production; the Bakken share is real but unverified barrel by barrel, so no Bakken flow is printed.

demand.label: Storage change (balancing line)
demand.source: Computed residual in the house balance build; shell bounds from Enbridge factsheets
demand.note: Storage is the printed balancing line of this balance, computed as the residual when the balance is run; it is never a measured input. Sanity bound: Clearbrook shell about 1.3 MMbbl plus Berthold about 0.7 MMbbl. No public Bakken stock series exists; PADD 2 stocks are the closest held aggregate.

groups.label: Core Four Counties
groups.source: RBN Energy (share); ND DMR county file (held, computable)
groups.note: McKenzie, Dunn, Mountrail and Williams counties produce nearly 90% of North Dakota output. The exact split is computable from the held DMR county file and is not yet computed, so no group value is printed.

groups.label: Guernsey sink
groups.source: Dossier sections 4-5; Kinder Morgan conversion record (Oct 2026 sweep)
groups.note: The southern optionality view: Butte inbound, Pony Express (about 460, to about 515 in late 2027) and Platte (145 to Wood River) outbound. Space is contested with Powder River, DJ and Canadian Express barrels. Double H no longer belongs in this group: Kinder Morgan took it out of crude service in early Q3 2025 for the Hiland Express NGL conversion (NGL service from Apr 29, 2026), and its crude barrels moved to Butte. Butte publishes no flows, so the group carries no value.

groups.label: Clearbrook and Mainline complex
groups.note: The Canadian-interaction view and the bridge to the WCSB page: Bakken barrels entering the Mainline at Cromer or Clearbrook compete for the same apportioned space as Canadian light. This is the same physical constraint the WCSB balance prints as apportionment, seen from the south side.

groups.label: Patoka and Gulf corridor
groups.source: FERC Form 6 Schedule 600 sample parse (held, micro_balances/sources/ferc_form6/)
groups.note: The growth and litigation view. Dakota Access carries the value; the ETCO onward split is not yet verified, so the group prints no separate total.

groups.label: Rail complex
groups.note: The swing view, priced off destination netbacks. Total rail out of PADD 2 origins was about 170 kb/d in Jul 2026, against a Dec 2014 peak of about 830-850.

groups.label: In-basin refining
groups.source: Dossier section 7; EIA-820 refinery capacity file, Jan 1 2026
groups.note: The firm-demand floor is one refinery: Mandan at 72 kb/d (EIA-820 calendar-day) is about 6% of supply and consumes no long-haul egress. Dickinson is gone from the crude system: it stopped processing crude in May 2020 and operates as Marathon's renewable diesel facility, so it carries no crude demand.

prices.label: Clearbrook differential to WTI (CMA)
prices.source: Argus and Platts assessments (paid series, not held)
prices.note: No assessed Clearbrook series is held, and no current print is invented. Documented episodes from the dossier: Dec 2013 WTI averaged $13.40/bbl over Clearbrook; sampled 2016-17 weeks printed about WTI minus $0.70 to minus $1.90; Oct-Nov 2018 blew out to roughly a $14.75-17.00 discount; Dec 2018 firmed to about minus $5.00. In a pipe-long basin the differential sits near the tariff-adjusted value of the marginal pipe route; excursions are the tightness signal.

storage.source: Enbridge Energy Infrastructure Assets factsheet (shell capacities)
storage.note: Shell capacity at the two northern hubs: Clearbrook about 1.3 MMbbl plus Berthold about 0.7 MMbbl. Cromer shell (about 2.4 MMbbl) sits in the Canadian frame. There is no public Bakken crude stock series, so no level is printed; storage enters the balance as the computed residual bounded by shell.

corridors.label: Stanley to Patoka to Nederland
corridors.from: Stanley and Johnson's Corner, North Dakota
corridors.note: Marketed as one Bakken system (Dakota Access plus ETCO).

corridors.label: Beaver Lodge to Clearbrook to Superior
corridors.note: Onward on the Mainline and Lakehead system; the Minnesota Pipe Line leg to Pine Bend is cited at 455 kb/d (2014 vintage).

corridors.label: Berthold to Cromer (Mainline)
corridors.note: Barrels join the Mainline light pool at Cromer and compete with Canadian light for apportioned space.

corridors.label: Guernsey to Cushing (Pony Express)
corridors.note: Pony Express about 460 kb/d average annual, PXP2 expansion to about 515 due late 2027. Platte runs Guernsey to Wood River at 145. Double H formerly shared this corridor; it left crude service in 2025 for the Hiland Express NGL conversion (in service Apr 29, 2026).

notes: Demand in this feed is CLEARED demand, not wants: the demand card equals supply less storage change by the house convention. East Daley's template prints wants (their Canada demand exceeded both supply and effective capacity); we do not copy that. Nominations are carried only where a source publishes them.

The demand card (1,233) does not foot to the valued demand items (781: Dakota Access 611 plus rail 170) because only Dakota Access and the rail lanes publish flows. The remaining roughly 452 kb/d clears on Enbridge ND, Bakken North, Butte and the Mandan refinery, whose monthly flows are not published by anyone. That is a publication gap, not a balance gap, and it is the normal state of this basin: Form 6 is annual and filer-level, so monthly pipe flows are modelled in every public treatment, including East Daley's.

Effective capacity (1,205) is an explicit estimate: nameplate (1,259) less the same roughly 4% routine maintenance and derate haircut applied in the October 2026 feed. No carrier publishes an effective figure for the system; the dossier flags it as an estimate to be replaced by shipper-notice history.
Utilization card is null: the only hard utilization is Dakota Access at 81% (CY2024 Form 6). A system figure would be an estimate (the dossier's range is roughly 75-85%) and is not printed as a card.
Exports card is null: exports equal cleared demand minus in-region refining (about 1,161 on this frame), but the dossier does not print that split as a card and the feed does not derive one silently.

The basin's real governor in growth months is gas, not pipe: North Dakota's 91% gas-capture rule (NDIC Order 24665) restricts wells to 200 bbl/d of oil at 60% capture and 100 bbl/d below that, so gas gathering and processing capacity in the core counties caps oil before egress does.

Supply must be re-bought monthly: legacy decline runs about 6% of production per month, so holding 1.16 MMb/d flat needs roughly 70-100 kb/d of new-well production every month. The rig count (31, Oct 2026, NDIC Director's Cut dated Oct 20, 2026, held activity file) and completion crews are the leading indicators, not the well count.

Dickinson carries no crude demand in this feed: Marathon's Dickinson plant (ex-Dakota Prairie, about 19 kb/d of crude capacity) stopped processing crude in May 2020 and was converted to a renewable diesel facility (184 MM gal/yr, fully operational 2021). It is absent from the EIA-820 crude capacity file dated Jan 1, 2026, which lists Mandan as North Dakota's only crude refinery. Earlier editions of this feed carried Dickinson at 19-20 kb/d of crude demand; that was stale and is removed.

Double H carries no crude egress in this feed: Kinder Morgan took the line out of crude service in early Q3 2025 for the Hiland Express NGL conversion, and it entered NGL service on Apr 29, 2026. Its crude barrels moved to Butte. Earlier editions carried Double H as an 84-99 kb/d crude range; that was stale and is removed, and system nameplate falls from 1,358 to 1,259 kb/d as a result.
